name: pcre2
notes: Next in the porting matrix expansion queue after bzip2/xz (see TODO.md's "Porting matrix expansion" bullet). No dependencies -- pcre2's regex engine is self-contained.

Scoped to the 8-bit code unit width only (--enable-pcre2-16/--enable-pcre2-32 both left off, matching the library's own default): every foreseeable future consumer in this queue (curl, and likely mbedtls if it ever needs pattern matching) only needs plain `char*` regex, not UTF-16/UTF-32 code units.

target_overrides.windows.cflags undefines _WIN32/_WIN32_WCE/__WIN32__/WIN32, the same technique already used for zlib.json/xz.json/bzip2.json, for the same reason: pcre2grep.c has a real `#include <windows.h>` + `FindFirstFile()`-based directory-walking implementation gated on WIN32 that this sysroot has no equivalent for (it is a Bionic-style POSIX libc, not a Windows SDK header set) -- undefining these keeps pcre2 (both the library and pcre2grep/pcre2test, which this recipe still builds since upstream's Makefile.am has no configure-time toggle to skip them) on its portable opendir()/readdir()-based POSIX path instead, which this project's own libc already supports. The core library's own pcre2.h.generic PCRE2_EXP_DECL macro also branches on _WIN32 for __declspec(dllimport) annotations -- undefining it means pcre2's own exported symbols rely on GNU ld/lld's auto-import extension for the shared build, same as libffi's ffi_type_* globals did; this project's Windows PAL now implements the required runtime pseudo-relocation fixup generally (libc/src/arch/windows/common/pseudo_reloc.c, see HISTORY.md's 2026-08-12 entry).

target_overrides.windows.configure_args adds --build=@CRT_MINGW_TRIPLE@, the same config.guess workaround already needed by libpng.json/xz.json/libffi.json: pcre2's configure is real GNU Autoconf output, and config.guess does not recognize plain Windows `uname` output.

The recipe test (porting/tests/pcre2_match_test.c, a real pcre2_compile()/pcre2_match() round trip with three capture groups, not just a version-string smoke check) initially failed to link on Windows with 'undefined symbol: __declspec(dllimport) pcre2_compile_8 ... cannot be used because it is not an import library': the LIBRARY itself was built with _WIN32 undefined (so its own exported symbols have no dllimport/dllexport decoration, correct for static linking), but the test file's own compile step is a separate crt-cc invocation that does NOT inherit target_overrides.windows.env.CFLAGS (that only applies to the library's own build), so it saw clang's default-predefined _WIN32 and expected DLL-import-style symbols against a plain static archive. Fixed with the standard, upstream-documented convention for exactly this situation: `-DPCRE2_STATIC` in the `match-static` test's own `cflags` (deliberately NOT applied to `match-shared`, since linking against the DLL's import library `libpcre2-8.dll.a` needs the default dllimport-decorated declarations, matching the artifact being linked).

Started static-only (`--disable-shared --enable-static`), matching this queue's own established caution (bzip2/xz both landed static-only first) -- once the static build/test passed for real on both Windows and Linux, removed that restriction (configure_args: [], matching zlib.json's own pattern of just letting the library's real default -- both static and shared -- apply) and added a `match-shared` test entry. libtool produces `libpcre2-8-0.dll` + `libpcre2-8.dll.a` (import library) on Windows, `libpcre2-8.so`(`.0`) on Linux, `libpcre2-8.dylib` on macOS.

Verified for real, not just 'it built': both `match-static` and `match-shared` print `pcre2_match_test: ok matches=4 version=10.47 2025-10-21` -- three named capture groups (user/host/tld) individually verified against the matched substrings, not just a nonzero match count -- on Windows (`cmake --build --preset windows-host-ninja-debug --target port-test-pcre2`), Linux (WSL Ubuntu 20.04 + clang-18, `tools/crt-port-build.py --port pcre2 --test`), and macOS (real aarch64 hardware, user-run). All three hosts: `shared-pass`.

macOS pitfall worth recording: the first attempt at `match-shared` there failed with `clang: error: no such file or directory: '.../lib/libpcre2-8.dylib'`, purely because `port-test-pcre2` reuses whatever is already installed under the `installed` stamp -- the user's install dir still held the *earlier*, static-only build from before this recipe dropped `--disable-shared`, so `libpcre2-8.dylib` genuinely didn't exist yet. Not a code bug: `cmake --build --preset <preset> --target port-rebuild-pcre2` (which clears the stamp and reruns configure/make/install) before `port-test-pcre2` picked up the new shared build correctly. Same caveat applies to any recipe whose `build.configure_args`/`env` changes after it was last built -- the stamp-based skip is deliberate (avoids re-running a slow `./configure && make` on every invocation) but does mean a recipe edit needs an explicit `port-rebuild-<name>` to actually take effect against an already-installed port.
